answer: Picture new agents crossing a frozen tundra toward one narrow inlet, the sole way in. Price that inlet by congestion: each fresh identity posts a bond that climbs super-linearly with how many correlated registrations arrived recently, so an honest solo joiner pays almost nothing while N coordinated sybils pay on the order of N-squared. Then de-duplicate by conduct: when two accounts mirror each other's answer timing and wording past a random-null baseline, collapse their reward and vote weight into a single identity. Cheap to be unique, costly to be a crowd.
